title: Taurine Deficiency & Longevity
subtitle: Circulating Taurine Decline as a Conserved Driver of Aging Across Worms, Mice, Monkeys, and Humans
summary: Circulating taurine drops by ~80% in elderly humans. Restoring youthful taurine levels (1,000 mg/kg/day) in middle-aged mice extended median lifespan by 10–12% and life expectancy at 28 months by 18–25%, improved bone, metabolic, and immune health in rhesus monkeys, and inversely tracked with diabetes, obesity, and inflammation across 11,966 humans.
modelSystem: C57BL/6J Mice, Rhesus Monkeys & n = 11,966 Humans

title: Genetics vs. Caloric Restriction & Fasting
subtitle: Dietary Restriction Impacts Health and Lifespan of 960 Genetically Diverse Mice
summary: Comparing Ad Libitum, 1-day/week IF, 2-day/week IF, 20% CR, and 40% CR across 960 genetically diverse Diversity Outbred mice reveals that genetics explains ~3x more lifespan variance (23.6%) than diet (~7.4–8.4%), 40% CR extends median lifespan by +36.3% (+9.2 months) at the cost of lean mass and immunity, and stress resilience—not weight loss—predicts longevity.
authors: Di Francesco, A. et al. (Churchill Lab)
tag: CR vs. IF in Genetic Diversity
modelSystem: Diversity Outbred (DO) Female Mice (5 Diet Arms)

title: VO2max & Long-Term All-Cause Mortality
subtitle: Cardiorespiratory Fitness Exhibits an Inverse, Dose-Dependent Mortality Reduction With No Upper Ceiling in 122,007 Adults
summary: In 122,007 adults undergoing symptom-limited exercise treadmill testing over 1.1 million person-years of follow-up, cardiorespiratory fitness showed a progressive survival advantage with no upper limit of harm: Low fitness (<25th percentile) carried a 5.04x higher mortality risk than Elite fitness (≥97.7th percentile, HR 0.20)—outweighing smoking, diabetes, or coronary artery disease.
authors: Mandsager, K. et al. (Jaber Lab, Cleveland Clinic)
modelSystem: Human Exercise Treadmill Cohort (Ages 18–80+)

title: Spermidine & Fasting-Induced Autophagy
subtitle: Endogenous Spermidine and eIF5A Hypusination Are Essential for Fasting-Mediated Autophagy and Longevity
summary: Across yeast, flies, mice, and 4 human fasting cohorts, caloric restriction and intermittent fasting surge endogenous polyamine spermidine levels (~40–50%). Blocking polyamine synthesis (via DFMO or genetics) abolishes fasting-induced autophagy, TFEB translation, cardioprotection, and lifespan extension—proving spermidine→eIF5A hypusination is the master metabolic switch of fasting.
authors: Hofer, S.J. et al. (Madeo & Kroemer Labs)
modelSystem: 4 Human Fasting Cohorts + Mice, Flies, Worms & Yeast

title: GlyNAC RCT: Glutathione & Mitophagy
subtitle: Supplementing Glycine and N-Acetylcysteine in Older Adults Restores Glutathione, Mitophagy, and Physical Function
summary: In a 16-week double-blind placebo-controlled human RCT, oral GlyNAC (100 mg/kg/day each of glycine and N-acetylcysteine) restored intracellular RBC glutathione by +164%, lowered lipid peroxidation (TBARS) by -72% and insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) by -64%, rescued mitochondrial fatty-acid oxidation, and improved gait speed to young-adult levels.
journal: J. Gerontol. A Biol. Sci. Med. Sci.
authors: Kumar, P. et al. (Sekhar Lab, Baylor)
modelSystem: Human Double-Blind Placebo-Controlled RCT (Ages 61–80)
sampleSize: n = 24 Older Adults (16 Wk) + n = 12 Young Controls

title: DO-HEALTH: Omega-3, Vitamin D & Exercise
subtitle: Individual and Additive Effects of Vitamin D, Omega-3 and Exercise on DNA Methylation Clocks in 777 Older Adults
summary: In a 3-year multicenter 2×2×2 factorial RCT of 777 older adults (≥70 yr), 1 g/day algae omega-3 alone slowed PC-PhenoAge, GrimAge2, and DunedinPACE, while combining omega-3, 2,000 IU/day vitamin D3, and home exercise additively slowed biological aging by 2.9–3.8 months.
authors: Bischoff-Ferrari, H.A., Horvath, S. et al.
modelSystem: Human 2×2×2 Factorial RCT (Adults ≥70 yr)

title: Trametinib + Rapamycin Synergy
subtitle: Dual Ras–MEK–ERK and mTORC1 Inhibition Additively Extends Mammalian Healthspan and Lifespan
summary: Combining the clinical MEK1/2 inhibitor trametinib with intermittent rapamycin in 875 C3B6F1 mice extended median lifespan by +34.9% in females and +27.4% in males—far surpassing either monotherapy while blocking age-related brain glucose hypermetabolism and liver tumors.
modelSystem: C3B6F1 Hybrid Mice (Male & Female from 6 mo)

title: Nonlinear Multi-Omic Aging Waves
subtitle: Longitudinal Profiling of 135,239 Biological Features Reveals Sharp Molecular Transitions at Ages 44 and 60
summary: Tracking 5,405 multi-tissue samples across 10 omics layers in 108 humans (aged 25–75) shows that 81.03% of molecules shift nonlinearly, cresting in two major systemic waves around age 44 (lipid, alcohol/caffeine & CVD pathways) and age 60 (immune, renal & carbohydrate regulation).
modelSystem: Longitudinal Human Multi-Omic Cohort (25–75 yr)

title: CALERIE™ RCT: Caloric Restriction & Pace of Aging
subtitle: Two Years of Human Caloric Restriction Slows the DunedinPACE Epigenetic Speedometer of Biological Aging
summary: In the 2-year Phase 2 CALERIE™ RCT of 220 non-obese adults quantified by doubly labeled water, caloric restriction significantly slowed the dynamic DunedinPACE speedometer by 2–3% (d = -0.25 to -0.29; d = -0.40 at 20% CR), corresponding to a 10–15% reduction in mortality risk.
modelSystem: Human Phase 2 RCT (25% Prescribed CR, 24 Months)

title: Organ-Specific Proteomic Clocks
subtitle: Organ-Specific Proteomic Aging Clocks Predict Disease and Longevity Across Diverse Populations
summary: Your body doesn't age at a single rate. Olink plasma proteomics across 48,393 humans (UK, China, USA) establishes 10 organ-specific clocks, showing that 5+ extremely aged organs increase mortality risk by 7.8x while 5+ super-youthful organs reduce dementia risk by 75%.
authors: Wang, Y., Xiao, S., Liu, B. et al.
modelSystem: Human Proteomic Cohorts (UKB, CKB China, US NHS)

title: Caloric Restriction vs. Exercise
subtitle: Distinct Systemic & Epigenetic Signatures of Long-Term Lifestyle Interventions in Humans
summary: A 6-layer multi-omic comparison in long-term human practitioners shows caloric restriction lowers clinical blood PhenoAge acceleration (-2.96 years) and mTOR/insulin signaling, whereas endurance exercise uniquely reduces colon mucosal Horvath epigenetic age (-2.25 years) and stochastic epigenetic mutation load (-4.91 years).
modelSystem: Human Multi-Omic Cohort (CR vs. Endurance Exercise)

title: IL-11 Inhibition & Lifespan
subtitle: Blocking Pro-Inflammatory IL-11 Signaling Extends Mammalian Healthspan and Lifespan
summary: Progressive upregulation of the pro-inflammatory cytokine IL-11 drives multi-organ fibrosis, sarcopenia, and metabolic decline via ERK–AMPK–mTORC1 signaling. Anti-IL-11 therapy initiated in 75-week-old mice extended median lifespan by 22.5% in males and 24.9% in females while reducing age-related tumors.
authors: Widjaja, A.A. et al. (Cook & Schafer Labs)
modelSystem: Aged C57BL/6J Mice (From 75 Weeks) & Il11 KO

title: Endogenous Longevity Metabolites
subtitle: How Declining Endogenous Metabolites Influence Aging and What Replenishment Can Achieve
summary: A comprehensive synthesis of 9 endogenous metabolites—including NAD+ precursors, Alpha-Ketoglutarate, Taurine, Spermidine, and Urolithin A—whose systemic decline accelerates the hallmarks of aging, contrasting rodent lifespan extension (AKG, Taurine) with human clinical healthspan biomarkers.
modelSystem: Cross-Species Review (Worms, Flies, Mice, Humans)

title: CAR T-Cell Senolytics
subtitle: Prophylactic and Therapeutic Living Senolytics Targeting uPAR in Aging and Metabolic Dysfunction
summary: Engineered CAR T-cells targeting the senescence-specific surface receptor uPAR act as a 'living drug': a single infusion clears senescent pancreatic, hepatic, and adipose cells in aged and high-fat-diet mice, restoring glucose tolerance and persisting for over a year.
modelSystem: Aged & HFD Mice (uPAR-Targeted CAR T Cells)

title: PF4 Systemic Rejuvenation
subtitle: Platelet Factor 4 as the Shared Messenger of Young Blood, Klotho, and Exercise in Brain Rejuvenation
summary: Three simultaneous Nature Portfolio papers (Schroer et al., Park et al., Leiter et al.) identify Platelet Factor 4 (PF4/CXCL4) as the converging exerkine and blood factor that attenuates neuroinflammation via CXCR3, enhances synaptic plasticity, and restores hippocampal cognition.
authors: Schroer et al.; Park et al.; Leiter et al.
modelSystem: Aged Mice (Young Blood, Klotho & Exercise Triad)

title: Epigenetic Reprogramming
subtitle: Loss of Epigenetic Information as a Causal Driver of Mammalian Aging and Reversal via OSK
summary: Using inducible non-mutagenic DNA breaks (ICE mice), Yang et al. prove that relocalization of chromatin modifiers (RCM) drives mammalian aging without DNA mutations—and that partial Yamanaka reprogramming (AAV-OSK, excluding oncogenic c-Myc) reverses epigenetic age by up to 57%.
modelSystem: Inducible ICE Mice & AAV-OSK Reprogramming

title: Rapamycin & mTOR Inhibition
subtitle: Late-Life Pharmacological Inhibition of mTORC1 Extends Lifespan in Genetically Heterogeneous Mice
summary: Initiated at 600 days of age (~60 human years) across three independent NIA ITP sites, microencapsulated rapamycin inhibited mTORC1 to extend overall maximum lifespan (+14% females, +9% males) and remaining life expectancy (+38% females, +28% males).
modelSystem: Genetically Heterogeneous UM-HET3 Mice (600 Days)
sampleSize: n = 1,901 Mice Across 3 NIA ITP Sites

title: Urolithin A & Mitophagy
subtitle: Selective Clearance of Dysfunctional Mitochondria Extends Worm Lifespan and Restores Rodent Muscle Function
summary: Direct supplementation with the postbiotic Urolithin A bypasses gut microbiome conversion bottlenecks to activate PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy, extending C. elegans lifespan by 45.4% and boosting running endurance by 42% in aged mice, with subsequent validation in human RCTs.
modelSystem: C. elegans, Aged C57BL/6J Mice & Human RCTs

title: NAD+ & Nuclear-Mitochondrial Sync
subtitle: Declining Nuclear NAD+ Induces a HIF-1α Pseudohypoxic State That Disrupts OXPHOS Prior to Structural Decay
summary: Age-related nuclear NAD+ depletion inactivates SIRT1, stabilizing HIF-1α under normoxia ('pseudohypoxia') and blocking c-Myc/TFAM transcription of mitochondrial OXPHOS genes. One week of NMN administration in 22-month-old mice restored muscle bioenergetics to 6-month-old levels.
modelSystem: Aged C57BL/6J Mice (22 Months -> 6 Months State)

title: Dasatinib + Quercetin Senolytics
subtitle: Senescent Cells Actively Drive Physical Frailty and Late-Life Intermittent Clearance Extends Remaining Survival
summary: Transplanting just 1 million senescent cells into young mice induces systemic frailty, while intermittent 'hit-and-run' clearance of senescent cells using Dasatinib + Quercetin in 24–27-month-old mice extends post-treatment survival by 36% without compressing late-life morbidity.
modelSystem: Very Old Mice (24–27 Months) & Human Adipose Explants

title: Metformin & Metabolic Hormesis
subtitle: Low-Dose Complex I Hormesis Extends Lifespan in C57BL/6 Mice While High Doses Prove Nephrotoxic
summary: Chronic low-dose metformin (0.1% w/w) mildly inhibits mitochondrial Complex I to activate AMPK and Nrf2 antioxidant defenses, extending mean lifespan by 5.83% in male C57BL/6 mice, whereas a 10-fold higher dose (1% w/w) causes fatal nephrotoxicity (-14.4% lifespan).
authors: Martin-Montalvo, A. et al. (de Cabo Lab)
modelSystem: Middle-Aged Male C57BL/6 Mice (0.1% vs 1% w/w)
